# Operations

<!-- Generated by `pnpm gen` from the op registry (packages/ops/src/ops). Do not edit; `pnpm gen:check` fails when stale. -->

The operation API (spec 6.3, ADR-003): every mutation and query of a document goes through these ops, over MCP, the CLI, `pf check` and (M2) `__pf.run`. Contract: additive changes only.

Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px. References: animations by `{"group", "direction"}` or `{"id"}`, frames by 0-based index or id, layers, bones, parts, views and variants by name or id (an id match wins; an ambiguous name is `AMBIGUOUS`).

## Results

A call returns `{"ok": true, "op", "output", "doc"?, "warnings"?}` or `{"ok": false, "op", "error"}`. `doc` is `{id, version, undoEntry, canUndo, canRedo}` for ops on a document. `warnings` (present only when non-empty) lists problems that happened **after** the change was committed, such as a change listener of the document throwing: the op succeeded, the change is applied and in `doc.undoEntry`.

Over MCP (`pf mcp`, `tools/list` carries no `outputSchema`) a success is that envelope as compact JSON in a text block; an output with a top-level `image` also returns an `image` content block and its `data` is left out of the text. A failure is a tool result with `isError: true` whose text is the error object `{"code", "message", "details"}`; it is never a protocol error.

## Safety classes

| Class | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | Changes nothing. |
| `mutate` | One transaction on one document = one undo step, labelled `AI: <op>`. |
| `destructive` | Like `mutate`, and the caller must pass `"confirm": true`. |
| `io` | Reads or writes files through the host ports; may change its document once (one undo step). |

## Tool groups

Every op belongs to one group; `pf mcp --tools <groups>` (or `PF_TOOLS`) lists only the chosen ones (default: all).

| Group | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `core` | documents, frames, animations, layers, cels, import/export, renders, pixel grids, lint, undo |
| `rig` | bones, poses, presets, templates, parts and overrides |
| `palette` | palette editing, sorting, colour ramps, remaps, generation and skins |
| `convert` | turn a PNG image or a layer into pixel art (crop, grid, downscale, palette, dither) |

## Errors

Every failure is `{"code", "message", "details"}`, identical on every transport.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `BAD_INPUT` | The input fails the schema (`details.issues`: `{path, message}`). |
| `UNKNOWN_OP` | No op of that name. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | A reference does not resolve (`details.kind`, `details.ref`, `details.available`). |
| `AMBIGUOUS` | A name matches several entities (`details.candidates`); pass an id. |
| `CONFIRM_REQUIRED` | A destructive op was called without `"confirm": true`. |
| `REFUSED` | The document state refuses the request (`details.reason`). |
| `INVALID_VALUE` | A value the document model rejects (`details.reason` when known). |
| `NOT_ALLOWED` | A path outside the workspace roots. |
| `DOC_LOCKED` | Another process owns the document (`details.pid`). |
| `CONFLICT` | Clashes with the host state or the history. |
| `BAD_FILE` | The file cannot be read as what it claims to be (`details.cause`). |
| `IO_FAILED` | A file system call failed. |
| `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` | Not built yet. |
| `INTERNAL` | A bug; nothing was changed. |

## anim.create

Create an animation (group + optional direction) with empty frames of equal duration.

(group, direction) must be unique. Names: lower-case a-z 0-9 _ - up to 48 characters; omit direction for an undirected animation. Frames start empty: pose them with rig_set_pose, draw into them, or add more with frame_add. Use loop "once" for a one-shot such as a jump: in a "loop" the keys interpolate across the wrap, from the last frame to the first. For a flipped copy of a side animation use rig_mirror_animation.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `anim_create`
- CLI: `pf anim create`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `group` | string | yes | Animation group, e.g. "run". |
| `direction` | string | no | Direction, e.g. "side" (omit for undirected). |
| `loop` | "loop" \| "once" \| "pingpong" | no | "loop" (default), "once" or "pingpong". |
| `frames` | integer >= 1 | no | Number of empty frames (default 1). |
| `durationMs` | integer >= 1 | no | Duration of every frame in ms (default 100). |
| `angleQuantum` | number | no | Rig angle quantum, deg (a multiple of 0.25 that divides 360; default 1). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | Animation id. |
| `label` | string | yes | "group/direction", or "group" when undirected. |
| `frameIds` | string[] | yes | Frame ids in play order. |

### Examples

A 4-frame side run loop at 100 ms:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","group":"run","direction":"side","frames":4}
```

## anim.update

Rename an animation (group, direction), set its loop mode, angle quantum or post-passes.

(group, direction) must stay unique. Renaming the group of a source animation renames its mirrors too; a mirror's group cannot change on its own. Loop, angleQuantum and postPasses belong to the source: a mirror has none. null clears direction, angleQuantum or postPasses. The loop mode changes how keys interpolate at the ends: "loop" wraps from the last frame to the first, "once" and "pingpong" hold. Frame durations, markers, events: frame_set_meta.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `anim_update`
- CLI: `pf anim update`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `group` | string | no | New group name. |
| `direction` | string \| null | no | New direction; null makes it undirected. |
| `loop` | "loop" \| "once" \| "pingpong" | no | "loop", "once" or "pingpong". |
| `angleQuantum` | number \| null | no | Rig angle quantum, deg (multiple of 0.25 dividing 360); null restores the default. |
| `postPasses` | {removeOrphans, outline} \| null | no | Post-passes after the rig render: {removeOrphans: {}, outline: {color: [r,g,b,a], outsideOnly?, corners?}}; null removes them. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | Animation id. |
| `label` | string | yes | "group/direction" afterwards. |
| `changed` | string[] | yes | Fields that changed; empty when nothing did. |
| `mirrors` | string[] | yes | Labels of the mirror animations renamed with it. |

### Examples

Make the hero idle a ping-pong:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"loop":"pingpong"}
```

Output:

```json
{"animation":"anm_5q60kk","label":"default","changed":["loop"],"mirrors":[]}
```

## cel.link

Link a layer's cel to another frame's cel (mode "link"), make a linked cel independent ("unlink"), or link all identical cels ("linkIdentical").

A linked cel shows the same pixels as its target; links cross animations, one hop (a link to a link goes to its target). "link": animation, frame (the cel that becomes the link), source.frame (source.animation defaults to animation). "unlink" copies the pixels into the cel. "linkIdentical" links, per layer, every cel with identical pixels, offset and opacity to the first in document order. Pixel layers only: part layers have no cels.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `cel_link`
- CLI: `pf cel link`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `layer` | string | yes | Layer id ("lay_...") or layer name. |
| `mode` | "link" \| "unlink" \| "linkIdentical" | yes | What to do. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | no | link/unlink: animation of the cel. linkIdentical: limits the scan (default: all). |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | no | link/unlink: the cel's frame. |
| `source` | {animation, frame} | no | link: the frame whose cel is shown. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | "link" \| "unlink" \| "linkIdentical" | yes |  |
| `changed` | integer | yes | Cels that were linked or unlinked (0 for a no-op). |
| `imagesDeleted` | integer | yes | Images that nothing used any more. |

### Examples

Link the hero layer cels that have identical pixels:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","layer":"body","mode":"linkIdentical"}
```

## convert.apply

Run a convert recipe on a layer cel: replace it, add a layer, or make a variant contact sheet.

Source: the cel of "layer" at animation/frame. Without newLayer the result replaces the cel and must keep the canvas size (so no downscale or outline). With newLayer it is added aligned to the origin. Quantises to the active palette unless palette/colors is given. With variants the document is untouched: a new document holds the sheet, "tiles" says where each combination sits.

- Group: `convert`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `convert_apply`
- CLI: `pf convert apply`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | {"group": "idle"} |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | Frame: 0-based index or frame id ("frm_..."). |
| `layer` | string | yes | Layer id ("lay_...") or layer name. |
| `newLayer` | string | no | Add the result as a new layer of this name. |
| `recipe` | map of any | no | Advanced: a ConvertRecipe {version:1, crop?, background?, downscale?, cleanup?, quantize?}. Replaces crop..clean. |
| `crop` | integer >= 0[] | no | [x, y, w, h], source px. |
| `background` | "none" \| "key" \| "flood" \| "alpha" | no | key: all pixels near the corner colour. flood: only those joined to the border. |
| `tolerance` | integer >= 0 | no | key/flood: RGB distance (default 0). |
| `grid` | "auto" \| integer >= 2 | no | Upscaled pixel art: "auto" finds the cell, or give its px size. Not with width/height. |
| `width` | integer >= 1 | no | Target px; the other side keeps the aspect. |
| `height` | integer >= 1 | no | Target px, like width. |
| `method` | "box" \| "kcentroid" \| "nearest" \| "mode" | no | Default kcentroid (mode with grid). |
| `palette` | string \| string[] | no | Preset id (pico-8, sweetie-16, ...) or ["#rrggbb", ...]. |
| `colors` | integer >= 2 | no | Make a palette of this many colours. |
| `dither` | "none" \| "bayer2" \| "bayer4" \| "bayer8" \| "floyd-steinberg" | no | Dither mode (default none). |
| `strength` | number | no | Dither strength (default 1). |
| `outline` | boolean | no | Add a 1 px outline (canvas +2 px). |
| `clean` | boolean | no | Alpha cut and lone-pixel removal (default true). |
| `variants` | {method, dither, palette} | no | Run every combination (max 64). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layer` | string | no | Layer that holds the result. |
| `size` | {w, h} | no | Result size, px. |
| `sheetDoc` | string | no | Variants: the new document with the contact sheet. |
| `tiles` | {label, x, y, w, h}[] | no | Variants: label and position of each result on the sheet. |
| `palette` | {name, colors} | no |  |
| `steps` | string[] | yes | Size after each step, e.g. "downscale 32x32". |
| `grid` | string | no | Cell size used by the downscale, "WxH". |

### Examples

Variant grid: two dither modes on layer "body":

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"idle"},"frame":0,"layer":"body","variants":{"dither":["none","bayer4"]}}
```

## convert.imageToSprite

Turn a PNG into pixel art: crop, background, grid or size, palette, dither. Opens a new document.

PNG only. Steps run in order: crop, background, downscale (width/height or grid), clean, quantise (any of palette, colors, dither). Quantising adds the palette to the document. With variants each combination is a layer (the first is visible).

- Group: `convert`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `image_to_sprite`
- CLI: `pf convert image-to-sprite`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | string | yes | Absolute PNG path inside the workspace roots. |
| `name` | string | no | Document name (default: the file name). |
| `recipe` | map of any | no | Advanced: a ConvertRecipe {version:1, crop?, background?, downscale?, cleanup?, quantize?}. Replaces crop..clean. |
| `crop` | integer >= 0[] | no | [x, y, w, h], source px. |
| `background` | "none" \| "key" \| "flood" \| "alpha" | no | key: all pixels near the corner colour. flood: only those joined to the border. |
| `tolerance` | integer >= 0 | no | key/flood: RGB distance (default 0). |
| `grid` | "auto" \| integer >= 2 | no | Upscaled pixel art: "auto" finds the cell, or give its px size. Not with width/height. |
| `width` | integer >= 1 | no | Target px; the other side keeps the aspect. |
| `height` | integer >= 1 | no | Target px, like width. |
| `method` | "box" \| "kcentroid" \| "nearest" \| "mode" | no | Default kcentroid (mode with grid). |
| `palette` | string \| string[] | no | Preset id (pico-8, sweetie-16, ...) or ["#rrggbb", ...]. |
| `colors` | integer >= 2 | no | Make a palette of this many colours. |
| `dither` | "none" \| "bayer2" \| "bayer4" \| "bayer8" \| "floyd-steinberg" | no | Dither mode (default none). |
| `strength` | number | no | Dither strength (default 1). |
| `outline` | boolean | no | Add a 1 px outline (canvas +2 px). |
| `clean` | boolean | no | Alpha cut and lone-pixel removal (default true). |
| `variants` | {method, dither, palette} | no | Run every combination (max 64). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | The new document. |
| `canvas` | {w, h} | yes |  |
| `layers` | string[] | yes | Layer names. |
| `palette` | {name, colors} | no | Active palette, if quantised. |
| `steps` | string[] | yes | Size after each step, e.g. "downscale 32x32". |
| `grid` | string | no | Cell size used by the downscale, "WxH". |

### Examples

32 px tall, PICO-8 colours, Bayer dither:

```json
{"file":"/work/photo.png","height":32,"background":"flood","tolerance":40,"palette":"pico-8","dither":"bayer4"}
```

## doc.create

Create a new empty RGBA document (no layers, no animations) and open it. Save it with doc_save.

The origin defaults to the bottom-centre pixel of the canvas (where the feet go). For a sprite sheet make the canvas the size of one cell. Import art with import_file, apply a skeleton with rig_apply_template, add animations with anim_create. Use doc_set_color_mode for indexed colour. Nothing is on disk until doc_save with a path.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `doc_create`
- CLI: `pf doc create`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | no | Display name (default "untitled"). |
| `width` | integer >= 1 | yes | Canvas width, int px. |
| `height` | integer >= 1 | yes | Canvas height, int px. |
| `origin` | {x, y} | no | Origin pixel on the canvas, int px (default: bottom-centre). |
| `pixelsPerUnit` | number | no | Pixels per engine unit (default 16). |
| `idSeed` | integer >= 0 | no | Seed of the id generator (default: derived from the host clock). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id for the other ops. |
| `name` | string | yes | Display name. |
| `canvas` | {w, h} | yes | Canvas size, px. |
| `origin` | {x, y} | yes | Origin pixel. |

### Examples

A 48x48 canvas:

```json
{"name":"hero","width":48,"height":48}
```

## doc.open

Open a .pxf file and return its document id, which every other op takes as "doc".

Opening a file that is already open returns the same id (alreadyOpen: true) without re-reading it. Returns the id only: read layers, rig and animations with doc_summary next.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `doc_open`
- CLI: `pf doc open`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | Path of the .pxf file (absolute, inside the workspace roots). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id for the other ops. |
| `path` | string | yes | Normalised path. |
| `name` | string | yes | Document display name. |
| `alreadyOpen` | boolean | yes | True when the file was open already. |
| `warnings` | string[] | yes | Problems found while reading (e.g. a dropped render cache). |

### Examples

Open the synthetic hero:

```json
{"path":"/work/hero.pxf"}
```

Output:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","path":"/work/hero.pxf","name":"hero","alreadyOpen":false,"warnings":[]}
```

## doc.redo

Redo the newest undone change of the document (one history entry).

Re-applies the entry that the last undo reverted. A new change clears the redo entries. Nothing to redo is not an error: redone is false.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate` (manages the history itself, no transaction)
- MCP tool: `redo`
- CLI: `pf doc redo`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `redone` | boolean | yes | True when an entry was re-applied; false when there was nothing to redo. |
| `label` | any | yes | Label of the re-applied entry (for example "AI: rig.setPose"); null when nothing was redone. |

### Examples

Redo on a fresh open (nothing to redo):

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}
```

Output:

```json
{"redone":false,"label":null}
```

## doc.save

Save the document to its .pxf file, or to a new path (first save, save as).

Nothing reaches disk before this call. With doc alone it saves to the file the document came from; a document from doc_create needs path (absolute, inside the workspace roots). Writes a temp file and renames it over the target, so a crash never leaves a torn file. A new path takes the document's lock first (DOC_LOCKED if another process owns it). An existing file at a new path is refused unless overwrite is true. An unchanged document writes nothing, unless its file lacks a current render cache or has an older schema version.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `doc_save`
- CLI: `pf doc save`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `path` | string | no | Target .pxf path (absolute, inside the workspace roots). Default: the current path. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | Replace an existing file at a new path (default false). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | Normalised path saved to. |
| `wrote` | boolean | yes | False when the file was already what this save would write and nothing was written. |
| `bytes` | integer | yes | Size of the file written, bytes (0 when nothing was written). |
| `version` | integer | yes | Store version that was saved. |

### Examples

Save the hero under a new name:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","path":"/work/hero-v2.pxf"}
```

## doc.setColorMode

Switch the document between "rgba" and "indexed" pixels, and/or lock it to its palette.

Converting is exact: to "indexed" every colour must be an entry of the active palette (the first alpha-0 entry is the transparent index), else the call is refused and nothing changes; to "rgba" indices resolve through the palette. Both need an active palette. The lock does not recolour: run lint next (palette.offPalette judges the render).

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `doc_set_color_mode`
- CLI: `pf doc set-color-mode`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `colorMode` | "rgba" \| "indexed" | no | "rgba" or "indexed" (default: unchanged). |
| `paletteLocked` | boolean | no | Lock colours to the active palette (default: unchanged). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colorMode` | "rgba" \| "indexed" | yes | Mode afterwards. |
| `paletteLocked` | boolean | yes | Lock afterwards. |
| `converted` | integer | yes | Drawings (cels, variants, override images) converted. |

### Examples

Lock a document that has a palette to it:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","paletteLocked":true}
```

## doc.summary

Summarise an open document: canvas, palette, layers, rig (bones, parts, views) and animations.

Names in the result (bones, parts, layers, animation group/direction) are what the other tools take as references. It shows no rest angles and no pose keys: for pivots and tips as numbers use render_frame with bones: true.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `read`
- MCP tool: `doc_summary`
- CLI: `pf doc summary`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id. |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `path` | any | yes | Backing file, null for an unsaved document. |
| `version` | integer | yes | Runtime version: +1 per change, undo and redo. |
| `dirty` | boolean | yes | Changed (or undone/redone) since it was opened or last saved. |
| `canUndo` | boolean | yes |  |
| `canRedo` | boolean | yes |  |
| `canvas` | {w, h} | yes |  |
| `origin` | {x, y} | yes | Anchor pixel shared with the engine (mirroring flips about origin.x). |
| `pixelsPerUnit` | number | yes |  |
| `colorMode` | "rgba" \| "indexed" | yes |  |
| `paletteLocked` | boolean | yes |  |
| `palette` | {name, colors} \| null | yes | The active palette, null when there is none. |
| `skins` | string[] | yes |  |
| `layers` | {id, path, kind, visible}[] | yes | Every layer, depth first, bottom to top. |
| `rig` | {bones, parts, views} \| null | yes | Null when the document has no rig. |
| `animations` | {id, label, group, direction, loop, frames, durationMs, mirrorOf, overrides}[] | yes |  |

### Examples

Summarise the hero:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}
```

## doc.undo

Undo the newest applied change of the document (one history entry).

Reverts the last applied history entry, whatever tool made it. Nothing to undo is not an error: undone is false. Re-apply with redo.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate` (manages the history itself, no transaction)
- MCP tool: `undo`
- CLI: `pf doc undo`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `undone` | boolean | yes | True when an entry was reverted; false when there was nothing to undo. |
| `label` | any | yes | Label of the reverted entry (for example "AI: rig.setPose"); null when nothing was undone. |

### Examples

Undo the last change of the hero (nothing to undo on a fresh open):

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}
```

Output:

```json
{"undone":false,"label":null}
```

## frame.add

Insert an empty frame before or after a frame; the new frame gets no bone or part keys.

The new frame has no keys, so bones and parts interpolate into it from the neighbouring keys. Cels and overrides are not copied (frame_duplicate copies them). Set its keys with rig_set_pose.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `frame_add`
- CLI: `pf frame add`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | Reference frame: the new frame goes next to it. |
| `position` | "before" \| "after" | no | "after" (default) inserts behind the reference frame, "before" in front of it. |
| `durationMs` | integer >= 1 | no | Duration of the new frame in ms (default: the reference frame duration). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frameId` | string | yes | Id of the new frame. |
| `frameIndex` | integer | yes | Index of the new frame in the animation. |
| `frames` | integer | yes | Frame count of the animation afterwards. |

### Examples

Add an empty frame after frame 0 of the hero:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0}
```

Output:

```json
{"frameId":"frm_j83g8j","frameIndex":1,"frames":2}
```

## frame.delete

Delete one frame with its bone and part keys, cels and overrides; the last frame cannot go.

Links to the frame's cels are materialised first: the other linked frames keep their picture as their own copy. Images nothing references any more are removed. Later frames move down one index. An animation keeps at least one frame.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `frame_delete`
- CLI: `pf frame delete`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | Frame: 0-based index or frame id ("frm_..."). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frameId` | string | yes | Id of the deleted frame. |
| `frames` | integer | yes | Frame count of the animation afterwards. |

### Examples

Delete frame 1 of the hero (add a second frame first; the hero has one):

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":1}
```

Output:

```json
{"frameId":"frm_j83g8j","frames":1}
```

## frame.duplicate

Duplicate one frame; the copy goes right after it, with linked cels and copied keys.

Cels of the copy link to the source frame (edit one, both change). Bone keys, part keys, markers, events, root motion, duration and overrides are copied, so the copy starts from the same pose: change it with rig_set_pose.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `frame_duplicate`
- CLI: `pf frame duplicate`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | Frame: 0-based index or frame id ("frm_..."). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frameId` | string | yes | Id of the new frame. |
| `frameIndex` | integer | yes | Index of the new frame (source index + 1). |
| `frames` | integer | yes | Frame count of the animation afterwards. |

### Examples

Duplicate frame 0 of the hero:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0}
```

Output:

```json
{"frameId":"frm_j83g8j","frameIndex":1,"frames":2}
```

## frame.setMeta

Set one frame's duration (ms), markers (name -> int px), events (names) and root motion (int px).

Only the fields you give change, on this one frame. markers merge by name (null removes one); events replace the whole list; rootMotion is the move the game applies when this frame plays (int px, y down). New marker and event names join the document's markerDefs / eventDefs. Mirror animations have no frames: edit the source.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `frame_set_meta`
- CLI: `pf frame set-meta`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | Frame: 0-based index or frame id ("frm_..."). |
| `durationMs` | integer >= 1 | no | Frame duration, ms. |
| `markers` | map of {x, y} \| null | no | Markers by name, canvas px (e.g. "hand_r": {"x": 30, "y": 20}); null removes one. |
| `events` | string[] | no | Event names fired on this frame; replaces the list. |
| `rootMotion` | {dx, dy} | no | Root motion of this frame, int px. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | "group/direction" of the animation. |
| `frameIndex` | integer | yes |  |
| `frameId` | string | yes |  |
| `changed` | string[] | yes | Fields that changed; empty when nothing did. |

### Examples

Hold the hero frame 200 ms and fire a footstep event:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"durationMs":200,"events":["footstep"]}
```

## io.export

Export animations as a spritesheet PNG plus a JSON description (Aseprite hash format).

Renders every frame like the game would see it (export layers only; rig, overrides and post-passes applied; mirrors flipped) and writes <name>.png and <name>.json side by side, atomically. layout "rows" puts one animation per row; "packed" fills a near-square grid. scale is an integer 1..16. The JSON lists a frame per cell with its duration, and one tag per animation. skin renders one skin; allSkins writes one sheet per skin (base, then each skin) with the same layout: <name>.png, <name>.<skin>.png. To look at art use render_contact_sheet instead; a scale 1 export of one animation is the base for override_import.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `export`
- CLI: `pf export`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `path` | string | yes | Output path (absolute, inside the workspace roots). .png: sheet, JSON beside it. .gif: one animation (give animations if several), loop from the animation, up to 256 colours. |
| `animations` | {group, direction} \| {id}[] | no | Animations to export, in order (default: all). |
| `layout` | "rows" \| "packed" | no | "rows" (default) or "packed". |
| `scale` | integer >= 1 | no | Integer scale, 1..16 (default 1). |
| `skin` | string | no | Skin name, or "base" (default). |
| `allSkins` | boolean | no | One sheet per skin: base as <name>.png, each skin as <name>.<skin>.png. |
| `exportOnly` | boolean | no | Only layers with export: true (default true). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `png` | string | no | Path of the written PNG. |
| `json` | string | no | Path of the written JSON. |
| `gif` | string | no | Path of the written GIF (.gif paths only). |
| `size` | {w, h} | yes | Sheet size, px. |
| `frames` | integer | yes | Frames exported. |
| `animations` | string[] | yes | Animation tags in sheet order. |
| `sheets` | {skin, png, json}[] | no | allSkins: every sheet written, base first. |

### Examples

Export the hero as a 2x sheet:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","path":"/work/out/hero.png","scale":2}
```

Output:

```json
{"png":"/work/out/hero.png","json":"/work/out/hero.json","size":{"w":96,"h":96},"frames":1,"animations":["default"]}
```

## io.import

Import a PNG spritesheet (cells per animation), a GIF (one frame per GIF frame) or an .aseprite file into a document.

Spritesheet: animations maps cells to animations; repeated cells become linked cels; the cell's bottom-centre lands on the document origin. To keep the sheet as a reference, import the frame to cut again as its own animation and layer. GIF: a new animation, one frame per GIF frame with its delay (0 gives defaultDurationMs); the GIF is placed like one cell. Aseprite: run rig_apply_template first or part layers stay unbound; adds layers, tags (as animations) and the palette; the canvas must equal the document's.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `import_file`
- CLI: `pf import`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `file` | string | yes | Path of the file (absolute, inside the workspace roots). |
| `format` | "spritesheet" \| "aseprite" \| "gif" | no | Default: from the file extension. |
| `cell` | array | no | spritesheet: cell size [w, h] px (default: the whole image is one cell). |
| `animations` | {group, direction, cells, durationMs, fps, loop}[] | no | spritesheet: the animations to cut (required for a spritesheet). |
| `outlineFile` | string | no | spritesheet: matching outline sheet, same size. |
| `layerName` | string | no | spritesheet, gif: layer for the cels (default "body"; reused if it exists). |
| `group` | string | no | gif: animation group (default "gif"). |
| `outlineLayerName` | string | no | spritesheet: layer of the outline sheet (default "outline"). |
| `defaultDurationMs` | integer >= 1 | no | spritesheet, gif: frame duration when none is given (default 100). |
| `reimport` | boolean | no | aseprite: update a file imported earlier instead of adding (default false). |
| `view` | string | no | aseprite: rig view for "part:" layers without #view (default: the first). |
| `paletteName` | string | no | aseprite: name of the imported palette. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | "spritesheet" \| "aseprite" \| "gif" | yes |  |
| `animations` | string[] | yes | Animations created or matched, as "group/direction". |
| `layers` | string[] | yes | Layers that received the pixels (names). |
| `frames` | integer | yes | Frames created (re-import: frames in the file). |
| `images` | integer | yes | Images created. |
| `parts` | {bound, updated, unbound} | no | aseprite: "part:" layers bound, updated (re-import) or left as pixel layers. |
| `warnings` | string[] | yes | Non-fatal findings. |

### Examples

Cut row 0, columns 0 to 2 of a 64x64 sheet into move_gather at 12 fps:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","file":"/work/run.png","cell":[64,64],"animations":[{"group":"move_gather","cells":[{"row":0,"col":"0-2"}],"fps":12}]}
```

## layer.update

Rename a layer, or set its visible flag, opacity (0..255) or export flag.

Only the fields you give change. Names are lower-case a-z 0-9 _ - up to 48 characters and unique among siblings; a part layer's name is the part's name and must be unique in the document. A reference layer is never exported. Hidden or non-exported layers are skipped by export, lint and rig_bake. To hide a part on some frames only, key visible with rig_set_pose.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `layer_update`
- CLI: `pf layer update`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `layer` | string | yes | Layer id ("lay_...") or layer name. |
| `name` | string | no | New layer name. |
| `visible` | boolean | no | Show or hide the layer in the editor render. |
| `opacity` | integer >= 0 | no | Layer opacity, 0..255. |
| `export` | boolean | no | Include the layer in exports and bakes. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layer` | string | yes | Layer id. |
| `path` | string | yes | Name path from the root afterwards (e.g. "body/arm"). |
| `changed` | string[] | yes | Fields that changed; empty when nothing did. |

### Examples

Hide the hero's head part from the editor render:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","layer":"head","visible":false}
```

## lint.run

Lint the document: palette, orphan pixels, joint gaps, stale overrides, empty frames, clipping, holes.

Sorted by rule, then document order. Narrow with enable, disable, animations or skins. "error" means a broken invariant; fix warnings before delivery. pixels.clipped: part art cut off at the canvas edge. rig.partHole: 1 px holes in rotated parts. count 0 is not a visual pass (jointGap checks rest only): see render_contact_sheet.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `read`
- MCP tool: `lint`
- CLI: `pf lint`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `enable` | "palette.offPalette" \| "palette.opacityInLocked" \| "pixels.orphan" \| "pixels.clipped" \| "rig.jointGap" \| "rig.partHole" \| "rig.staleOverride" \| "rig.overrideError" \| "rig.rotationResidual" \| "anim.emptyFrame" \| "lint.renderError"[] | no | Run only these rule ids (default: all). |
| `disable` | "palette.offPalette" \| "palette.opacityInLocked" \| "pixels.orphan" \| "pixels.clipped" \| "rig.jointGap" \| "rig.partHole" \| "rig.staleOverride" \| "rig.overrideError" \| "rig.rotationResidual" \| "anim.emptyFrame" \| "lint.renderError"[] | no | Skip these rule ids (applied after enable). |
| `animations` | {group, direction} \| {id}[] | no | Animations to render and check (default: all, in document order). |
| `skins` | string[] | no | Skin names to render for palette checks; "base" is the base colours (default: base, then every skin). |
| `maxPixels` | integer >= 1 | no | Most pixels listed per finding (default 16). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | integer | yes | Number of findings. |
| `findings` | {rule, severity, location, message, data}[] | yes | The findings, in report order. |

### Examples

Lint the hero, joint and palette rules only:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","enable":["rig.jointGap","palette.offPalette"]}
```

## override.import

Import an edited PNG of a rig frame: the pixels that differ from the render become overrides.

Touch-up path: export the frame (export, scale 1, one animation), edit the PNG, import it. The PNG must be canvas-sized; it is compared with the exported render. Each changed stroke becomes a part override when one part owns it, else a final one, and survives re-posing. `newlyStale` lists earlier overrides it made stale: see override_list. Needs a rig; palette-locked and indexed documents only take palette colours.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `override_import`
- CLI: `pf override import`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | Frame: 0-based index or frame id ("frm_..."). |
| `file` | string | yes | The edited PNG (absolute, inside the workspace roots), canvas size, scale 1. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | "group/direction" of the animation edited. |
| `frameIndex` | integer | yes | 0-based index of the frame edited. |
| `changed` | integer | yes | Pixels that differ from the render (0: nothing was written). |
| `overrides` | string[] | yes | Ids of the overrides created, in order. |
| `newlyStale` | string[] | yes | Ids of earlier overrides this import made stale (still applied). |

### Examples

Import the touched-up frame 2 of the run animation:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"run","direction":"side"},"frame":2,"file":"/work/run-2-edited.png"}
```

## override.list

List overrides: stale ones (art under them changed) and ones that fail to render, apart.

Renders the frames that have overrides. "stale" overrides are still applied; decide with override_resolve (keep, rebase = accept the current art, discard). "errors" cannot be judged because their frame does not render (missing image, no view for the direction...): fix the rig first, they cannot be rebased until it renders. Part overrides of mirror animations are never rendered and not listed.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `read`
- MCP tool: `override_list`
- CLI: `pf override list`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animations` | {group, direction} \| {id}[] | no | Only these animations (default: all). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `counts` | {total, valid, stale, errors} | yes |  |
| `stale` | {id, animation, frameIndex, frameId, target, mirror, reason, errorCode, errorMessage}[] | yes | Stale overrides (reason "hash" or "no-target"). |
| `errors` | {id, animation, frameIndex, frameId, target, mirror, reason, errorCode, errorMessage}[] | yes | Overrides whose render failed (reason "error"). |
| `valid` | string[] | yes | Ids of the overrides that are up to date. |

### Examples

List the hero overrides:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}
```

## override.resolve

Resolve overrides: "keep" them, "rebase" onto the current art, or "discard" them.

Name overrides by id (from override_list) or pass allStale: true. "keep" changes nothing (a stale override is still applied) and just confirms the ids exist. "rebase" accepts the art under the override as the new base, so it stops being stale; the frame must render. "discard" deletes the override and its pixels. With allStale, overrides that fail to render or have no target are left out of a rebase and listed in skipped. Check the frame with render_frame after a discard.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `override_resolve`
- CLI: `pf override resolve`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `action` | "keep" \| "rebase" \| "discard" | yes | What to do with them. |
| `overrides` | string[] | no | Override ids ("ovr_..."). |
| `allStale` | boolean | no | Also include every stale override of the document (default false). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | "keep" \| "rebase" \| "discard" | yes |  |
| `resolved` | string[] | yes | Override ids the action applied to. |
| `skipped` | string[] | yes | allStale rebase: ids left out because they fail to render or have no target. |

### Examples

Re-base every stale override after reviewing the render:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","action":"rebase","allStale":true}
```

Output:

```json
{"action":"rebase","resolved":[],"skipped":[]}
```

## palette.edit

Add, remove, replace or move colours of the active palette.

Edits apply in order; indices refer to the palette as earlier edits left it. Indexed documents: pixels and skins follow moves; removing a colour pixels still use is refused. Replace recolours indexed pixels. With no palette, add creates one.

- Group: `palette`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `palette_edit`
- CLI: `pf palette edit`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `edits` | any[] | yes | Edits, in order. |
| `name` | string | no | Name for a palette this call creates. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `palette` | string | yes | Palette id. |
| `colors` | string[] | yes | The colours afterwards, "#rrggbb[aa]". |
| `remap` | any[] | no | New index of each old index (null: removed); omitted when nothing moved. |
| `images` | integer | yes | Indexed drawings rewritten. |
| `warning` | string | no |  |

### Examples

Add a dark outline colour, then recolour entry 2:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","edits":[{"do":"add","color":"#1a1c2c"},{"do":"replace","index":2,"color":"#b13e53"}]}
```

## palette.generate

Make a palette of N colours from an image (k-means++ in OKLab or median cut); optionally keep it.

Source: "file" (a PNG) or "animation"+"frame" (rendered; "layer" = one cel). Seeded: same image, method and seed give the same colours everywhere. Alpha 0 pixels are ignored, others count by their RGB; colours come out opaque, darkest first, and occur in the image. With n or fewer distinct colours you get those (fewer than n). Without add: true it only returns them; add stores a NEW palette (activate: also make it active; refused for an indexed document, whose pixels would change colour).

- Group: `palette`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `palette_generate`
- CLI: `pf palette generate`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `n` | integer >= 2 | yes | Colours wanted, 2 to 256. |
| `file` | string | no | Source: absolute path of a PNG inside the workspace roots. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | no | Source: the animation to take a frame from (instead of "file"). |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | no | With animation: the frame (default 0). |
| `layer` | string | no | With animation: use this pixel layer's cel instead of the whole rendered frame. |
| `method` | "kmeans" \| "mediancut" | no | "kmeans" (default): k-means++ in OKLab. "mediancut": splits colour boxes; ignores seed. |
| `seed` | integer >= 0 | no | Random seed of kmeans (default 1). |
| `minAlpha` | integer >= 1 | no | Ignore pixels with alpha below this (default 1: only fully transparent pixels). |
| `add` | boolean | no | Store the colours as a new palette of the document (default false: only return them). |
| `activate` | boolean | no | With add: make it the active palette (default: only when the document has none). |
| `name` | string | no | With add: palette name (default "generated"). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colors` | string[] | yes | The palette, darkest first, "#rrggbb". |
| `method` | "kmeans" \| "mediancut" | yes |  |
| `seed` | integer | no | Seed used (kmeans). |
| `source` | "file" \| "frame" \| "layer" | yes | Where the pixels came from. |
| `pixels` | integer | yes | Pixels that counted. |
| `ignored` | integer | yes | Pixels ignored (alpha below minAlpha). |
| `unique` | integer | yes | Distinct colours among the counted pixels. |
| `palette` | string | no | Id of the stored palette (with add). |
| `active` | boolean | no | True when the stored palette is now active (with add). |
| `note` | string | no | Set when fewer colours than n were found or colours were merged. |

### Examples

16 colours from frame 0, kept as a new palette:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","n":16,"animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"add":true,"name":"sprite16"}
```

## palette.ramp

Generate a dark-to-light colour ramp from a base colour; optionally add it.

OKLab ramp, step 0 darkest. Shadows turn toward blue, lights toward yellow by up to hueShift degrees; the base colour stays exact at baseIndex. Without add: true it only returns the colours. add inserts them (at, default the end) and records a named ramp; an indexed document keeps its pixels.

- Group: `palette`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `palette_ramp`
- CLI: `pf palette ramp`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `base` | string | yes | Base colour. |
| `steps` | integer >= 1 | yes | Colours in the ramp. |
| `baseIndex` | integer >= 0 | no | Where the base sits (default: middle). |
| `hueShift` | number | no | Largest hue turn at the ends, degrees (default 20; 0 = none). |
| `satShift` | number | no | Chroma change at the ends: shadows x(1-s), lights x(1+s) (default 0). |
| `lightRange` | array | no | OKLab lightness [darkest, lightest] (default from the base). |
| `coolHue` | number | no | Shadow hue target, OKLCH degrees (default 265). |
| `warmHue` | number | no | Light hue target, OKLCH degrees (default 90). |
| `add` | boolean | no | Add the ramp to the active palette (default false: only return it). |
| `at` | integer >= 0 | no | With add: insert here (default: the end). |
| `name` | string | no | With add: ramp name (default "ramp1", "ramp2"...). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colors` | string[] | yes | The ramp, dark to light, "#rrggbb[aa]". |
| `indices` | integer[] | no | Palette indices of the new colours (with add). |
| `ramp` | string | no | Name of the recorded ramp (with add). |
| `warning` | string | no |  |

### Examples

A 5-colour skin ramp, added to the palette:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","base":"#c8503c","steps":5,"add":true,"name":"skin"}
```

## palette.remap

Recolour drawings with a mapping table, or swap the palette colours.

Give map or swap. map: [{from,to}] by palette index (indexed document) or exact "#rrggbb[aa]" (RGBA); applied at once, unlisted and transparent pixels stay. Scope: all drawings, or layer and/or animation+frames (cels only). swap: {palette: id} or {colors: [...]} of the same length replaces the active colours, indices stay. Locked RGBA: a map target off the palette is refused.

- Group: `palette`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `palette_remap`
- CLI: `pf palette remap`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `map` | {from, to}[] | no | Mapping table. |
| `swap` | {palette, colors} | no | Replace the active palette colours. Whole document only. |
| `layer` | string | no | map: only this pixel layer. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | no | map: only the cels of this animation (with frames). |
| `frames` | integer >= 0 \| string[] | no | map: only these frames. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | "map" \| "swap" | yes |  |
| `changed` | integer | yes | Pixels changed in all drawings. |
| `drawings` | {where, changed}[] | yes | Drawings that changed, with their changed pixels. |
| `scanned` | integer | yes | Drawings looked at. |
| `palette` | string | no | swap: palette id. |
| `colors` | string[] | no | swap: the colours afterwards. |

### Examples

Indexed: move red (3) to blue (5) in one layer:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","map":[{"from":3,"to":5}],"layer":"Body"}
```

Swap in a team palette of the same length:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","swap":{"colors":["#00000000","#1a1c2c","#b13e53"]}}
```

## palette.sort

Sort the active palette by hue, luminance, luma or chroma.

Stable: equal keys keep their order. luminance = OKLab lightness, luma = Rec. 709 on 8-bit sRGB, hue puts greys first. Indexed documents: pixels, ramps and skins follow the colours.

- Group: `palette`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `palette_sort`
- CLI: `pf palette sort`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `by` | "hue" \| "luminance" \| "luma" \| "chroma" | yes | Sort key. |
| `descending` | boolean | no | Largest first (default false). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `order` | integer[] | yes | order[newIndex] = oldIndex. |
| `images` | integer | yes | Indexed drawings rewritten. |
| `warning` | string | no |  |

### Examples

Dark to light:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","by":"luminance"}
```

## part.paintOverlap

Close joint gaps by painting hidden overlap on the part drawn lower; the rest composite stays the same.

For each joint with gaps (rig_joint_check), paints only pixels the upper part covers at rest, growing the variant image and shifting its pivot to keep the part in place. One flat colour: the variant's most frequent opaque one, or color. At big bends it shows as a patch with no outline, so check the pose. "uncovered" lists joints no hidden paint can close; "skipped" joints with several parts per bone or a part rotated at rest. Run rig_joint_check next.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `part_paint_overlap`
- CLI: `pf part paint-overlap`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `view` | string | no | Rig view to check (default: the first view). |
| `bones` | string[] | no | Only joints whose child bone is one of these (default: all joints with gaps). |
| `color` | array \| integer >= 0 | no | Paint colour: [r,g,b,a], or a palette index in an indexed document. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `painted` | {part, variant, bones, pixels, grew, pivot}[] | yes | Variants that were painted (empty when no joint has gaps). |
| `uncovered` | {bone, pixels}[] | yes | Joints with gap pixels no hidden paint can close. |
| `skipped` | {bone, parent, reason}[] | yes | Joints the helper cannot handle. |

### Examples

Close the elbow gap of the hero:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","bones":["lower_arm_r"]}
```

## part.paintVariant

Paint a text grid into a part variant's own image.

"." transparent, "_" keeps. x, y are in the variant image; negative grows it (the pivot moves, the part stays put). Fixes a cut for every pose. Frame overrides of the part go stale (override_list). Locked palettes: palette colours only.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `part_paint_variant`
- CLI: `pf part paint-variant`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `part` | string | yes | Part: its part-layer name (e.g. "head"), part id ("prt_...") or layer id. |
| `variant` | string | no | Variant name (e.g. "default", "sleeve") or id ("var_..."). |
| `x` | integer | no | Column of the grid in the variant image (default 0). |
| `y` | integer | no | Row (default 0). |
| `rows` | string[] | yes | Equal-length rows, at most 32x32 symbols. |
| `legend` | map of string | yes | Symbol (0-9A-Za-z) to "#rrggbb[aa]". |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `part` | string | yes | Part layer name. |
| `variant` | string | yes | Variant id. |
| `changed` | integer | yes | Pixels whose colour changed (0: nothing was written). |
| `grew` | {left, top, right, bottom} | yes | Pixels the image grew on each side. |
| `pivot` | {x, y} | yes | Pivot afterwards. |

### Examples

Restore two forearm pixels:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","part":"lower_arm_r","x":0,"y":0,"rows":["11"],"legend":{"1":"#e8be96"}}
```

## part.split

Split a region (rect, lasso or flood) of a flat layer's cel into a new layer bound to a bone.

Fit the bones first: the part keeps the bone pivot of this moment. partName ("part:upper_arm_r") binds it, else overlap, else it stays a pixel layer. The part draws in every frame of every animation: key visible false (rig_set_pose) where other art shows. Refused: rig-block-order (a pixel layer covers the part), duplicate-variant (a second cut into one part: undo, recut it whole).

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `part_split`
- CLI: `pf part split`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `layer` | string | yes | The flat pixel layer to cut from (id or name). |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | The frame whose cel is cut. |
| `selection` | any | yes | The region to cut. |
| `partName` | string | no | Bind as "part:<bone>[.<part>][@variant][#view]" or a bone name. |
| `name` | string | no | Name of the new layer while it is not a part (default "split"). |
| `bind` | boolean | no | Without partName: try to bind by overlap (default true). |
| `view` | string | no | View for names without #view and for overlap (default: the first). |
| `zByBone` | map of integer | no | Default z of the new part by part-layer name, then bone name; higher draws on top. Set at creation; change later with rig_set_part_z. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layer` | string | yes | Layer holding the moved pixels (the part layer once bound). |
| `image` | string | yes | Image id of the moved pixels. |
| `bounds` | {x, y, w, h} | yes | Canvas rectangle of the moved pixels. |
| `pixels` | integer | yes | Pixels moved. |
| `bound` | {part, variant, bone, view, how, merged} | no | Present when the layer became (part of) a part. |
| `ambiguous` | string[] | no | Bones tied for the overlap (nothing bound). |
| `skipped` | string | no | Why automatic binding was skipped (kebab-case). |
| `unlinked` | integer | yes | Other frames whose linked cel now owns the original drawing. |

### Examples

Cut the head rectangle of a flat run frame into the head part:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","layer":"body","animation":{"group":"run"},"frame":0,"selection":{"kind":"rect","x":24,"y":16,"w":18,"h":12},"partName":"part:head"}
```

## pixels.readGrid

Read a region (at most 64x64 px) of a frame as a text grid: one symbol per pixel, "." transparent, with a legend of the colours present.

Without "layer" the region is the rendered frame (what pixels_write_grid edits on a rig frame); with a pixel "layer" it is that cel. Symbols 0-9A-Za-z are assigned by first appearance and valid for this call only; at most 62 colours (else read less). "rulers" adds column and row numbers, about 2 characters per pixel in all: read only the area you need. Feed `rows` and `legend` to pixels_write_grid.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `read`
- MCP tool: `pixels_read_grid`
- CLI: `pf pixels read-grid`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | Frame: 0-based index or frame id ("frm_..."). |
| `layer` | string | no | Read this pixel layer's cel instead of the rendered frame (mirror animations: not allowed). |
| `x` | integer >= 0 | no | Left column of the region, canvas px (default 0). |
| `y` | integer >= 0 | no | Top row of the region, canvas px (default 0). |
| `width` | integer >= 1 | no | Region width, 1..64 px (default: to the right edge, if at most 64). |
| `height` | integer >= 1 | no | Region height, 1..64 px (default: to the bottom edge, if at most 64). |
| `rulers` | boolean | no | Also return `ruled`: the rows with column and row numbers (default false). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | "group/direction" of the animation read. |
| `frameIndex` | integer | yes | 0-based index of the frame read. |
| `source` | "render" \| "cel" | yes | "render": the rendered frame; "cel": one layer's cel. |
| `x` | integer | yes | Left column of the region, canvas px. |
| `y` | integer | yes | Top row of the region, canvas px. |
| `width` | integer | yes | Region width, px. |
| `height` | integer | yes | Region height, px. |
| `legend` | map of string | yes | Symbol to colour "#rrggbb" ("#rrggbbaa" when translucent), for this call only. "." (transparent) is not listed. |
| `rows` | string[] | yes | One string per pixel row, `width` symbols each. |
| `ruled` | string[] | no | Only with rulers: two header lines of column numbers, then each row prefixed by its row number. |

### Examples

Read the hero head, 8x6 px at (21, 0):

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"x":21,"y":0,"width":8,"height":6}
```

Output:

```json
{"animation":"default","frameIndex":0,"source":"render","x":21,"y":0,"width":8,"height":6,"legend":{"0":"#462d1e","1":"#e8be96","2":"#1e1e28"},"rows":["00000000","00000000","00000000","00111111","00111121","00111111"]}
```

## pixels.writeGrid

Paint a text grid (at most 32x32 px) at (x, y) of a frame; symbols come from "legend".

"." writes transparent, "_" keeps the pixel. On a rig omit layer: differences from the rendered frame become overrides of this frame only. They are for touch-ups of a few pixels: art pasted over a pose is not rig animation and goes stale when the pose changes. If the rig cannot show something, say so instead. A part layer is refused. On flat art name the pixel `layer`. Locked palettes only take palette colours.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `pixels_write_grid`
- CLI: `pf pixels write-grid`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | Frame: 0-based index or frame id ("frm_..."). |
| `layer` | string | no | Pixel layer whose cel to write. Omit on a rig frame (the rendered frame is edited into overrides), or when the document has exactly one pixel layer. |
| `x` | integer >= 0 | no | Canvas column of the grid's left edge (default 0). |
| `y` | integer >= 0 | no | Canvas row of the grid's top edge (default 0). |
| `rows` | string[] | yes | Pixel rows, at most 32 rows of at most 32 equally long symbols: "." transparent, "_" keep, 0-9A-Za-z from the legend. |
| `legend` | map of string | yes | Symbol (one of 0-9A-Za-z) to colour "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa". Only symbols used in `rows` need an entry. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | "group/direction" of the animation written. |
| `frameIndex` | integer | yes | 0-based index of the frame written. |
| `target` | "overrides" \| "cel" | yes | "overrides": rig frame, edits stored as overrides; "cel": a pixel layer cel was rewritten. |
| `changed` | integer | yes | Pixels whose colour changed (0: nothing was written). |
| `layer` | string | no | Name of the layer written; only for target "cel". |
| `overrides` | string[] | yes | Ids of the overrides created, in order; empty unless target is "overrides". |
| `newlyStale` | string[] | yes | Ids of earlier overrides this edit made stale (still applied; re-base or discard them). |

### Examples

Move the hero's eye one pixel left (an override on the head):

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"x":26,"y":4,"rows":["21"],"legend":{"1":"#e8be96","2":"#1e1e28"}}
```

## pxf.pack

Build a .pxf from a .pxfd folder (the inverse of pxf_unpack).

Packs manifest.json, document.json, images/ and render/ of the folder; .gdignore and other files are ignored. The archive is built by the same deterministic writer as a save, atomically, replacing an existing file. file defaults to the folder name with .pxf. Works on files, not on open documents: doc_open the result to validate it.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `pxf_pack`
- CLI: `pf pack`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | yes | The .pxfd folder (absolute, inside the workspace roots). |
| `file` | string | no | The .pxf to write, named *.pxf (default: beside the folder). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | yes | The folder that was read. |
| `file` | string | yes | The .pxf written. |

### Examples

Rebuild hero.pxf from its folder:

```json
{"dir":"/work/hero.pxfd"}
```

Output:

```json
{"dir":"/work/hero.pxfd","file":"/work/hero.pxf"}
```

## pxf.unpack

Expand a .pxf into a .pxfd folder (manifest, document, images, render cache).

Writes one file per archive entry (bytes verbatim) plus an empty .gdignore so Godot ignores the PNGs; the folder diffs well in git. dir defaults to the file name with .pxfd. An existing folder is refused unless overwrite is true (only a folder named *.pxfd is ever replaced). Works on the file, not on an open document: doc_save first. pxf_pack is the inverse.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `pxf_unpack`
- CLI: `pf unpack`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | string | yes | The .pxf to expand (absolute, inside the workspace roots). |
| `dir` | string | no | Folder to create, named *.pxfd (default: beside the file). |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | Replace an existing folder (default false). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | string | yes | The .pxf that was read. |
| `dir` | string | yes | The folder written. |

### Examples

Expand hero.pxf next to itself:

```json
{"file":"/work/hero.pxf"}
```

Output:

```json
{"file":"/work/hero.pxf","dir":"/work/hero.pxfd"}
```

## render.contactSheet

Render the frames of some or all animations as one labelled PNG contact sheet (long edge at most 1568 px), optionally with bone lines and pivot markers.

Judge motion across frames (before/after a re-pose, a walk cycle): vision judges gesture and readability, lint owns precision (1 px gaps, off-palette pixels). Check the tile edges: art past the canvas is cut off and lint does not report it. Tiles are labelled "GROUP/DIRECTION #n" (n = frame index). The scale is the largest that fits 1568 px, or lower than `scale`. `bones` draws yellow bone lines and `pivots` red pivot squares (need a rig).

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `read`
- MCP tool: `render_contact_sheet`
- CLI: `pf render contact-sheet`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animations` | {group, direction} \| {id}[] | no | Animations to show, in order (default: all). |
| `scale` | integer >= 1 | no | Integer upscale to start from, 1..16 (default: the largest that fits 1568 px; reduced until it fits). |
| `labels` | boolean | no | Write "GROUP/DIRECTION #n" under each frame (default true). |
| `skin` | string | no | Skin name or id ("skn_..."); omit for the base render. |
| `bones` | boolean | no | Draw a line from each bone pivot to its tip on every tile (default false). |
| `pivots` | boolean | no | Draw a marker on each bone pivot pixel on every tile (default false). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frames` | integer | yes | Number of frames on the sheet. |
| `columns` | integer | yes | Tiles per row. |
| `rows` | integer | yes | Tile rows. |
| `scale` | integer | yes | The upscale used. |
| `image` | {mimeType, data, width, height} | yes | The contact sheet PNG. |

### Examples

Show every frame of the hero with the skeleton drawn:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","bones":true,"pivots":true}
```

## render.frame

Render one frame to an upscaled PNG on a checkerboard (long edge at most 1568 px), optionally with bone lines and pivot markers.

Look at the result of an edit: vision judges gesture, proportions and readability, lint owns precision (1 px gaps, off-palette pixels). `bones` draws a yellow line from each bone pivot to its tip, `pivots` a red square on each pivot pixel (both need a rig). With either, `output.bones` lists pivots and tips as canvas numbers: how to read a posed skeleton. Transparent pixels show a grey checkerboard.

- Group: `core`
- Safety: `read`
- MCP tool: `render_frame`
- CLI: `pf render frame`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | Frame: 0-based index or frame id ("frm_..."). |
| `scale` | integer >= 1 | no | Integer upscale 1..16 (default and maximum: the largest that keeps the long edge within 1568 px). |
| `skin` | string | no | Skin name or id ("skn_..."); omit for the base render. |
| `bones` | boolean | no | Draw a line from each bone pivot to its tip (default false). |
| `pivots` | boolean | no | Draw a marker on each bone pivot pixel (default false). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | "group/direction" of the rendered animation. |
| `frameIndex` | integer | yes | 0-based index of the rendered frame. |
| `scale` | integer | yes | The upscale used (may be lower than requested to fit 1568 px). |
| `image` | {mimeType, data, width, height} | yes | The rendered PNG. |
| `bones` | {name, parent, pivot, tip}[] | no | The overlay bones in canvas pixels; present when bones or pivots was set. |

### Examples

Look at frame 0 of the hero with the skeleton drawn:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"scale":8,"bones":true,"pivots":true}
```

## rig.applyPreset

Generate a motion preset (walk, run, jump, idle-breathe, swing) as an animation.

Needs the humanoid template bone names. Writes animation <group>/side (group defaults to the preset); an existing one needs replace:true and loses its bone keys. Output: the resolved params, rootMotion and labels per frame. Next: render_contact_sheet.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `rig_apply_preset`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `preset` | string | yes | Preset name: idle-breathe, jump, run, swing, walk. |
| `params` | map of number | no | Numeric parameters (defaults in the output). |
| `group` | string | no | Default: the preset name. |
| `direction` | string | no | Default "side". |
| `frames` | integer | no | Same as params.frames. |
| `durationMs` | integer >= 1 | no | Frame ms (default 100). |
| `view` | string | no | Character view; only "side" (default). |
| `replace` | boolean | no | Overwrite an existing animation. |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `frames` | integer | yes | Frame count. |

| `params` | map of number | yes | Every parameter with defaults filled in. |
| `rootMotion` | {dx, dy}[] | yes | Root motion per frame, px (also stored on the frames). |
| `labels` | map of string[] | yes | Labels per frame, e.g. foot_l. |
| `warnings` | string[] | yes |  |
