
## rig.applyTemplate

Apply a humanoid skeleton template: bones matched by name are reused, missing ones are created.

Templates: humanoid-side (view "side"), humanoid-front ("front"), humanoid-back ("back"). Without view a new view is created (named after the template, or viewName); with view the rest pose is set there. The template origin is the document origin. Rest: pelvis -90 (up), limbs 180 relative to it (down). Proportions are generic: compare with render_frame (bones) and refit with rig_edit_bones before any part_split. Bones that exist with another parent are refused.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `rig_apply_template`
- CLI: `pf rig apply-template`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `template` | "humanoid-side" \| "humanoid-front" \| "humanoid-back" | yes | Skeleton template: humanoid-side, humanoid-front or humanoid-back. |
| `height` | integer >= 8 | no | Character height in px, feet row to top of head (default 48). |
| `view` | string | no | Existing view to set the rest pose in (default: a new view). |
| `viewName` | string | no | Name of the new view (default: the template name, e.g. "side"); ignored with view. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `viewId` | string | yes | Id of the view the template was applied to. |
| `bones` | map of string | yes | Bone id per template bone name (reused and created). |
| `created` | string[] | yes | Names of the bones that were created. |

### Examples

Set the rest pose of the hero in its existing side view:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","template":"humanoid-side","view":"side"}
```

## rig.bake

Bake a rig animation into one plain pixel layer: as a new animation, or in place.

Renders every frame (parts, overrides, post-passes, exported layers) into a pixel layer "baked" and hides the parts. mode "new" adds animation <group>_baked; "replace" bakes in place. A mirror cannot be baked: bake its source. Baked pixels no longer follow the rig.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `destructive`
- MCP tool: `rig_bake`
- CLI: `pf rig bake`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `mode` | "new" \| "replace" | yes | "new" keeps the source; "replace" bakes it in place. |
| `name` | string | no | mode "new": group of the baked animation (default <group>_baked). |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | Must be true: this operation is destructive. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | Id of the baked animation. |
| `layer` | string | yes | Id of the new pixel layer holding the baked pixels. |
| `frames` | string[] | yes | Frame ids of the baked animation, in play order. |
| `dropped` | {boneKeys, partKeys, overrides, postPasses, cels} | yes | What a "replace" bake removed (all zero for "new"). |

### Examples

Bake the hero idle as a new animation:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"mode":"new","confirm":true}
```

## rig.bindParts

Bind pixel layers to bones as parts, by layer name ("part:<bone>[.<part>][@variant][#view]") or by overlap.

By name: a layer called part:upper_arm_r (or just a bone name) becomes that bone's part; @variant adds a variant of the same part, #view another view. By overlap: remaining layers bind to the bone their opaque pixels cover, only with a clear winner (ties are listed as ambiguous). The part keeps the bone pivot of this moment: fit the bones first. Animated and translucent layers are skipped. Running it again changes nothing. Cut flat art with part_split.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `rig_bind_parts`
- CLI: `pf rig bind-parts`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `layers` | string[] | no | Only these layers (default: every pixel layer). |
| `byName` | boolean | no | Bind by layer name (default true). |
| `byOverlap` | boolean | no | Bind the rest by overlap with the bones (default true). |
| `rawNames` | map of string | no | Source names to parse instead of layer names, by layer: {"arm": "part:upper_arm_r@open#side"}. |
| `view` | string | no | View for names without #view and for overlap (default: the first). |
| `zByBone` | map of integer | no | Default z of new parts by part-layer name, then bone name; higher draws on top. Set at creation; change later with rig_set_part_z. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bound` | {layer, part, variant, bone, view, how, merged}[] | yes | Layers that became (part of) a part. |
| `ambiguous` | {layer, candidates}[] | yes | Layers whose overlap has no clear winner (left alone). |
| `skipped` | {layer, reason}[] | yes | Layers left alone, with the reason. |

### Examples

Bind every layer named after a bone, no overlap guessing:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","byOverlap":false}
```

## rig.editBones

Edit the skeleton: add/delete/reparent/rename bones, set length and rest pose per view, add/rename/delete views.

Edits run in order; one failure undoes all. A bone with parts or (without cascade) children cannot be deleted. Rest x/y: root = canvas pivot, child = canvas offset from the parent pivot. Rest angle adds to the parent's: world 0 = +x, 90 = down, so a thigh pointing down under a pelvis at -90 is 180. Returns no geometry: check with render_frame (bones).

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `rig_edit_bones`
- CLI: `pf rig edit-bones`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `edits` | any[] | yes | Edits, applied in order. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | {action, id}[] | yes | One entry per edit, in order. |
| `bones` | integer | yes | Bone count afterwards. |

### Examples

Fit a thigh: 2 px left of the pelvis pivot, pointing down:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","edits":[{"action":"setRest","bone":"thigh_l","view":"side","x":-2,"y":0,"angle":180},{"action":"setLength","bone":"thigh_l","length":8}]}
```

Add a tail bone under the torso, then lengthen the head:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","edits":[{"action":"addBone","name":"tail","parent":"torso","length":8},{"action":"setLength","bone":"head","length":9}]}
```

## rig.fitPose

Find the bone angles (deg, relative to rest) and part variants whose render of one frame matches a target image.

Target: file (PNG, canvas size) or targetFrame. Searches each bone angle within ±range and each listed part variant. Pass the output bones and parts to rig_set_pose to apply them. exact: no pixel differs; else error counts them. Seeded: the same input gives the same result. A miss is not proof that no pose fits: raise maxRenders or narrow range.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `io`
- MCP tool: `rig_fit_pose`
- CLI: `pf rig fit-pose`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | yes | The frame to pose; its other keys stay as they are. |
| `file` | string | no | Target PNG, the size of the canvas. |
| `targetFrame` | integer >= 0 \| string | no | Target: another frame of this animation, rendered. |
| `bones` | string[] | no | Bones whose angle to search (names or ids; default: every bone). |
| `parts` | string[] | no | Parts whose variant to search (default: none). |
| `range` | number | no | Search each angle within ±range deg of rest (default 180). |
| `seed` | integer | no | Seed of the random restarts (default 1). |
| `maxRenders` | integer >= 1 | no | Most renders (default 3000). |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | "group/direction" of the animation. |
| `frameIndex` | integer | yes | The frame that was fitted. |
| `exact` | boolean | yes | True when the render equals the target (error 0). |
| `error` | integer | yes | Pixels that differ from the target at the best pose. |
| `renders` | integer | yes | Renders used. |
| `bones` | map of {angle} | yes | Best angle by bone name: the bones input of rig_set_pose. |
| `parts` | map of {variant} | yes | Best variant by part name: the parts input of rig_set_pose. |

### Examples

Pose the right arm like a reference image:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"file":"/work/reference.png","bones":["upper_arm_r","lower_arm_r"],"parts":["lower_arm_r"]}
```

## rig.fitTemplate

Fit a humanoid template to landmark points: lengths and rest pose in one call.

Like rig_apply_template, but sizes the bones from landmarks (canvas px, arms hanging): headTop, hips, feet (between the soles; becomes the root), optional handL/handR fingertips. Existing bones are resized. Check with render_frame (bones), then touch up with rig_edit_bones.

| `template` | "humanoid-side" \| "humanoid-front" \| "humanoid-back" | yes | Skeleton template. |
| `landmarks` | {headTop, hips, feet, handL, handR} | yes | Landmarks in canvas px. |
| `view` | string | no | Existing view to set the rest pose in (default: new). |
| `viewName` | string | no | Name of the new view; ignored with view. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `viewId` | string | yes | Id of the view the fit was written to. |
| `height` | integer | yes | Character height, px. |

### Examples

Fit the side template to a 47 px character:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","template":"humanoid-side","view":"side","landmarks":{"headTop":{"x":31,"y":16},"hips":{"x":30,"y":44},"feet":{"x":30,"y":63},"handR":{"x":38,"y":47}}}
```

## rig.jointCheck

Sweep each joint of one rig view and report the pixel gaps that open on the outer side of a bend.

A rig passes when summary.gapCount is 0. The full output is about 400 characters per joint: pass compact for a short form, or use lint with enable ["rig.jointGap"] for pass or fail. The sweep moves one joint at a time, rangeDeg around rest (default 30): a pose beyond that is not checked, so look at the render. Fix gaps with part_paint_overlap, or by moving part pivots, then check again. Checks the view that draws the first direction of the given view (default: the first view).

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `read`
- MCP tool: `rig_joint_check`
- CLI: `pf rig joint-check`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `view` | string | no | Rig view to check (default: the first view). |
| `rangeDeg` | number | no | Sweep range, degrees either side of rest. |
| `stepDeg` | number | no | Sweep step, degrees. |
| `radius` | integer >= 1 | no | Window radius of the check, px. |
| `compact` | boolean | no | Short form: summary and problems, no joints. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `view` | string | yes | Name of the checked view. |
| `params` | {rangeDeg, stepDeg, radius} | yes |  |
| `joints` | {bone, parent, pivot, gapCount, union, angles}[] | no | One entry per joint, sorted by bone name. Absent when compact. |
| `problems` | {bone, kind, gapCount, unionCount}[] | no | Joints with gaps. Only when compact. |
| `summary` | {joints, jointsWithGaps, gapCount, unionCount} | yes |  |

### Examples

Check the first view of the hero:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}
```

## rig.mirrorAnimation

Add a mirror of an animation under a new direction: same group, flipped around the origin.

The mirror stores no frames or pixels: it plays the source flipped horizontally about the document origin (markers flip too, names stay), so later edits of the source carry over: pose the source, not the mirror. Asymmetric art needs a separate animation. The mirror takes the source's group and loop; the direction must be new for that group. A source cannot be a mirror itself. Final overrides of the mirror can be added with pixels_write_grid on it.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `rig_mirror_animation`
- CLI: `pf rig mirror-animation`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `source` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | The animation to mirror (an authored one, not itself a mirror). |
| `direction` | string | yes | Direction of the mirror, e.g. "left" for a "right" source. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | Id of the new mirror animation. |
| `label` | string | yes | "group/direction" of the mirror. |
| `mirrorOf` | string | yes | Label of the source. |

### Examples

Mirror the hero idle as its left-facing twin:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","source":{"group":"default"},"direction":"left"}
```

## rig.readPose

Read one frame: bone and part values, and which are real keys (the rest are interpolated or held).

Output matches rig_set_pose input: pass bones and parts back unchanged. Lists only bones and channels that some frame keys; the rest are at rest. keyed names the real keys on this frame ("bones.<name>.<channel>"); other values are interpolated or held. Writing a value back makes it a key: this frame renders the same, other frames may change, so write back only what you mean to key. Mirror animations: read the source.

| `frameIndex` | integer | yes |  |

## rig.setPivot

Set a part variant's pivot: the pixel (int px, in the variant image) that sits on the bone pivot.

Binding already puts the pivot on the bone: use this to shift a part against its bone. Coordinates are in the variant image, origin top-left, pixel centre; the pivot may lie outside the image (a floating hand). It moves the part's art relative to the bone, so do not nudge it to clear joint gaps: use part_paint_overlap. Run rig_joint_check next. Variant names repeat across views: pass view when the name is ambiguous.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `rig_set_pivot`
- CLI: `pf rig set-pivot`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `part` | string | yes | Part: its part-layer name (e.g. "head"), part id ("prt_...") or layer id. |
| `variant` | string | no | Variant name or id (default "default"). |
| `view` | string | no | Resolve the variant name among this view's variants. |
| `pivot` | {x, y} | yes | New pivot, int px in the variant image. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `part` | string | yes | Part layer name. |
| `variant` | string | yes | Variant id. |
| `pivot` | {x, y} | yes | Pivot afterwards. |
| `previous` | {x, y} | yes | Pivot before. |

### Examples

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","part":"lower_arm_r","pivot":{"x":3,"y":1}}
```

## rig.setPose

Set bone keys (angle deg clockwise, offset int px) and/or part keys (variant, z, visible) on one frame or many.

Channels you pass replace the stored ones; null removes a bone or part key. A channel not keyed here interpolates between keys on other frames, not to rest: key offsets on every frame or none. Part keys hold both ways: set z or visible once. "frames" poses many frames as one undo step. targets {bone:{x,y}}: IK sets parent angles (wins over bones, earlier targets); reached: within 1 px. Output keyed: bones keyed; interpolated: keyed elsewhere, not on a posed frame (keyAll keys them at rest). Off-canvas art is cut. Next: render_contact_sheet.

- Group: `rig`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `rig_set_pose`
- CLI: `pf rig set-pose`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `animation` | {group, direction} \| {id} | yes | Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}. |
| `frame` | integer >= 0 \| string | no | Frame: 0-based index or frame id ("frm_..."). |
| `bones` | map of {angle, offset, flipX, interp} \| null | no | Bone keys by bone name (or id); null removes the key. |
| `parts` | map of {variant, z, visible} \| null | no | Part keys by part-layer name (or part id); null removes the key. |
| `frames` | {frame, bones, parts, targets}[] | no | Many frames, instead of frame. |
| `targets` | map of {x, y, chain, bend} | no | End-effector targets by bone name (or id). |
| `keyAll` | boolean | no | Also key all other bones at rest on posed frames. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | string | yes | "group/direction" of the posed animation. |
| `frameIndex` | integer | yes | The posed frame; the first with "frames". |
| `frameId` | string | yes |  |
| `frames` | integer[] | no | Posed frame indexes, with "frames". |
| `changed` | string[] | yes | Keys that changed, as "bones.<name>" / "parts.<name>"; empty when nothing did. |
| `keyed` | string[] | yes | Bones this call keys. |
| `interpolated` | string[] | yes | Bones that interpolate on a posed frame. |
| `targets` | {frame, bone, target, effector, reached, keyed}[] | no | One entry per end-effector target. |

### Examples

Raise the right arm on frame 0:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"bones":{"upper_arm_r":{"angle":-45},"lower_arm_r":{"angle":-30}}}
```

Output:

```json
{"animation":"default","frameIndex":0,"frameId":"frm_j83g8j","changed":["bones.lower_arm_r","bones.upper_arm_r"],"keyed":["lower_arm_r","upper_arm_r"],"interpolated":[]}
```

Put the right hand at (24,30) by IK:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"targets":{"hand_r":{"x":24,"y":30}}}
```

Switch the forearm to its sleeve variant and drop the torso key:

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"run","direction":"side"},"frame":2,"bones":{"torso":null},"parts":{"lower_arm_r":{"variant":"sleeve"}}}
```

## skin.set

Create, replace or remove a skin (a recoloured render for team kits).

Name a skin and give exactly one of: map [{from,to}] (remap skin: palette index, or the exact colour of a palette entry), palette (id or name of another palette: palette skin), colors (new palette, same length as the active one), remove true. Same name replaces the skin. Skins never change pixels; render_frame, io.export (allSkins) and lint (palette.offPalette) apply them. Palette edits that move indices are refused while a palette skin exists.

- Group: `palette`
- Safety: `mutate`
- MCP tool: `skin_set`
- CLI: `pf skin set`

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id from doc_open or doc_create. |
| `skin` | string | yes | Skin name (a-z, 0-9, "-", "_"; not "base") or id. |
| `map` | {from, to}[] | no | Remap skin: index (or palette colour) from to to; applied at once. |
| `palette` | string | no | Palette skin: id or name of another palette. |
| `colors` | string[] | no | Palette skin: a new palette, one colour per active palette entry. |
| `remove` | true | no | Delete the skin. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `skin` | string | yes | Skin name. |
| `id` | string | yes | Skin id. |
| `action` | "created" \| "updated" \| "removed" | yes |  |
| `kind` | "remap" \| "palette" | no | Absent when removed. |
| `skins` | string[] | yes | All skin names afterwards. |
| `warnings` | string[] | no |  |

### Examples

A rival kit: swap the body colour (1) and the accent (4):

```json
{"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","skin":"rival","map":[{"from":1,"to":4},{"from":4,"to":1}]}
```
